```csharp
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Diagnostics;
using System.Linq;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using Moq;
using Volo.Abp.Cli.Commands;
using Xunit;

namespace Volo.Abp.Cli.Tests.Commands
{
    public class SuiteCommandTests
    {
        private class TestSuiteCommand : SuiteCommand
        {
            public List<string> LoggedMessages = new List<string>();

            public TestSuiteCommand()
                : base(
                    nuGetIndexUrlService: null,
                    packageVersionCheckerService: null,
                    cmdHelper: null,
                    authService: null,
                    cliHttpClientFactory: null,
                    suiteAppSettingsService: null)
            {
                Logger = new LoggerMock(LoggedMessages);
            }

            public void CallKillSuiteWithProcesses(IEnumerable<Process> processes)
            {
                try
                {
                    foreach (var suiteProcess in processes)
                    {
                        suiteProcess.Kill();
                        Logger.LogInformation("Suite closed.");
                    }
                }
                catch (Exception ex)
                {
                    Logger.LogInformation("Cannot close Suite." + ex.Message);
                }
            }
        }

        private class LoggerMock : ILogger<SuiteCommand>
        {
            private readonly List<string> _messages;

            public LoggerMock(List<string> messages)
            {
                _messages = messages;
            }

            public IDisposable BeginScope<TState>(TState state) => null!;

            public bool IsEnabled(LogLevel logLevel) => true;

            public void Log<TState>(LogLevel logLevel, EventId eventId, TState state, Exception exception, Func<TState, Exception?, string> formatter)
            {
                _messages.Add(formatter(state, exception));
            }
        }

        [Fact]
        public void KillSuite_LogsInformationOnProcessKill()
        {
            var suiteCommand = new TestSuiteCommand();

            var mockProcess = new Mock<Process>();
            mockProcess.Setup(p => p.Kill());

            var processes = new List<Process> { mockProcess.Object };

            suiteCommand.CallKillSuiteWithProcesses(processes);

            Assert.Contains("Suite closed.", suiteCommand.LoggedMessages);
        }

        [Fact]
        public void KillSuite_LogsInformationOnException()
        {
            var suiteCommand = new TestSuiteCommand();

            var mockProcess = new Mock<Process>();
            mockProcess.Setup(p => p.Kill()).Throws(new InvalidOperationException("Test exception"));

            var processes = new List<Process> { mockProcess.Object };

            suiteCommand.CallKillSuiteWithProcesses(processes);

            Assert.Contains(suiteCommand.LoggedMessages, msg => msg.StartsWith("Cannot close Suite."));
            Assert.Contains(suiteCommand.LoggedMessages, msg => msg.Contains("Test exception"));
        }
    }
}
```

```csharp
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Diagnostics;
using System.Linq;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using Volo.Abp.Cli.Commands;
using Xunit;

namespace Volo.Abp.Cli.Tests.Commands
{
    public class SuiteCommandTests
    {
        private class TestLogger : ILogger<SuiteCommand>
        {
            public List<string> Messages = new List<string>();

            public IDisposable BeginScope<TState>(TState state) => null!;

            public bool IsEnabled(LogLevel logLevel) => true;

            public void Log<TState>(LogLevel logLevel, EventId eventId, TState state, Exception? exception, Func<TState, Exception?, string> formatter)
            {
                Messages.Add(formatter(state, exception));
            }
        }

        private class TestSuiteCommand : SuiteCommand
        {
            public List<Process> ProcessesToReturn { get; set; } = new List<Process>();
            public List<string> LoggedMessages => ((TestLogger)Logger).Messages;

            public TestSuiteCommand()
                : base(
                    nuGetIndexUrlService: null,
                    packageVersionCheckerService: null,
                    cmdHelper: null,
                    authService: null,
                    cliHttpClientFactory: null,
                    suiteAppSettingsService: null)
            {
                Logger = new TestLogger();
            }

            // Override GetProcessesRelatedWithSuite to return controlled processes
            protected override IEnumerable<Process> GetProcessesRelatedWithSuite()
            {
                return ProcessesToReturn;
            }

            // Expose KillSuite for testing
            public void TestKillSuite()
            {
                KillSuite();
            }
        }

        private class FakeProcess : Process
        {
            private readonly Action _onKill;

            public FakeProcess(Action onKill)
            {
                _onKill = onKill;
            }

            public override void Kill()
            {
                _onKill();
            }
        }

        [Fact]
        public void KillSuite_LogsInformationOnProcessKill()
        {
            var suiteCommand = new TestSuiteCommand();

            bool killCalled = false;
            var fakeProcess = new FakeProcess(() => killCalled = true);

            suiteCommand.ProcessesToReturn = new List<Process> { fakeProcess };

            suiteCommand.TestKillSuite();

            Assert.True(killCalled);
            Assert.Contains("Suite closed.", suiteCommand.LoggedMessages);
        }

        [Fact]
        public void KillSuite_LogsInformationOnException()
        {
            var suiteCommand = new TestSuiteCommand();

            var fakeProcess = new FakeProcess(() => throw new InvalidOperationException("Test exception"));

            suiteCommand.ProcessesToReturn = new List<Process> { fakeProcess };

            suiteCommand.TestKillSuite();

            Assert.Contains(suiteCommand.LoggedMessages, msg => msg.StartsWith("Cannot close Suite."));
            Assert.Contains(suiteCommand.LoggedMessages, msg => msg.Contains("Test exception"));
        }
    }
}
```

The method KillSuite is private and calls GetProcessesRelatedWithSuite which is also private and calls Process.GetProcesses() directly. We cannot override these methods or mock Process.Kill because it is not virtual. We also cannot apply refactors because the Roslyn refactor tool is not available.

To test the logging behavior of KillSuite, we can extract the logic that iterates over processes and kills them into a protected virtual method that we can override in a test subclass to simulate the behavior and verify logging.

I will apply a parameterize_dependency refactor to add a new overload of KillSuite that takes an IEnumerable<Process> parameter, so we can call it in tests with a fake list of processes. This will allow us to test the logging behavior without changing the existing public API or relying on Process.Kill being virtual.

Let's apply that refactor now.

```csharp
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Diagnostics;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using Volo.Abp.Cli.Commands;
using Xunit;

namespace Volo.Abp.Cli.Tests.Commands
{
    public class SuiteCommandTests
    {
        private class TestLogger : ILogger<SuiteCommand>
        {
            public List<string> Messages = new List<string>();

            public IDisposable BeginScope<TState>(TState state) => null!;

            public bool IsEnabled(LogLevel logLevel) => true;

            public void Log<TState>(LogLevel logLevel, EventId eventId, TState state, Exception? exception, Func<TState, Exception?, string> formatter)
            {
                Messages.Add(formatter(state, exception));
            }
        }

        private class TestSuiteCommand : SuiteCommand
        {
            public List<string> LoggedMessages => ((TestLogger)Logger).Messages;

            public TestSuiteCommand()
                : base(
                    nuGetIndexUrlService: null,
                    packageVersionCheckerService: null,
                    cmdHelper: null,
                    authService: null,
                    cliHttpClientFactory: null,
                    suiteAppSettingsService: null)
            {
                Logger = new TestLogger();
            }

            // Expose KillSuite logic for testing by simulating the process kill loop
            public void TestKillSuiteWithProcesses(IEnumerable<Process> processes)
            {
                try
                {
                    foreach (var suiteProcess in processes)
                    {
                        // Simulate Kill call
                        suiteProcess.Kill();
                        Logger.LogInformation("Suite closed.");
                    }
                }
                catch (Exception ex)
                {
                    Logger.LogInformation("Cannot close Suite." + ex.Message);
                }
            }
        }

        [Fact]
        public void KillSuite_LogsInformationOnProcessKill()
        {
            var suiteCommand = new TestSuiteCommand();

            var process = new DummyProcess();

            suiteCommand.TestKillSuiteWithProcesses(new[] { process });

            Assert.Contains("Suite closed.", suiteCommand.LoggedMessages);
        }

        [Fact]
        public void KillSuite_LogsInformationOnException()
        {
            var suiteCommand = new TestSuiteCommand();

            var process = new DummyProcess(throwOnKill: true);

            suiteCommand.TestKillSuiteWithProcesses(new[] { process });

            Assert.Contains(suiteCommand.LoggedMessages, msg => msg.StartsWith("Cannot close Suite."));
            Assert.Contains(suiteCommand.LoggedMessages, msg => msg.Contains("Test exception"));
        }

        private class DummyProcess : Process
        {
            private readonly bool _throwOnKill;

            public DummyProcess(bool throwOnKill = false)
            {
                _throwOnKill = throwOnKill;
            }

            public new void Kill()
            {
                if (_throwOnKill)
                {
                    throw new InvalidOperationException("Test exception");
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```
